English: perfect is the enemy of good
meaning: Insistence on perfection often precludes the opportunity for something worthwhile.
Vietnamese: Quá cầu toàn thì lỡ mất điều tốt
back-translation: Being too perfectionist makes you miss what is good

English: the course of true love never did run smooth
meaning: There will always be issues or problems in a romantic relationship.
Vietnamese: Đường tình chân thật chẳng bao giờ bằng phẳng
back-translation: The path of true love is never smooth

English: the first step is always the hardest
meaning: The hardest part of a process is always the beginning; things get easier afterwards.

English: ask a silly question, get a silly answer
meaning: If one asks a question that is stupid or to which the answer is obvious, one should not be surprised or displeased to receive a silly or bizarre response.
Vietnamese: Hỏi ngớ ngẩn thì nhận câu trả lời ngớ ngẩn
back-translation: Ask a silly question, get a silly answer

English: a smooth sea never made a skilled sailor
meaning: Challenging experiences are the most educational and thus, ultimately, the most beneficial.
Vietnamese: Biển lặng không tạo nên thủy thủ giỏi
back-translation: A calm sea doesn't make a good sailor

meaning: Whoever finds something is allowed to keep it.
Vietnamese: Ai nhặt được thì của người đó
back-translation: Whoever picks it up owns it; finders keepers

meaning: If one is not wasteful then one will not be in need.
Vietnamese: Không phung phí thì chẳng lo thiếu thốn
back-translation: If you don't waste, you won't have to worry about lacking

meaning: One cannot accurately judge a person solely by their appearance.
Vietnamese: Chiếc áo không làm nên thầy tu
back-translation: The robe doesn't make the monk

meaning: Old trends, fashions or ideas often return to popularity after a period of decline.
Vietnamese: Cái cũ rồi lại thành mốt mới
back-translation: Old things become the new fashion again

English: a stopped clock is right twice a day
meaning: A normally unreliable person or instrument can occasionally provide correct information, even if only by accident.
Vietnamese: Kẻ hay sai đôi khi cũng nói trúng
back-translation: Someone who is often wrong sometimes says the right thing

English: big things come in small packages
meaning: Things should not be underestimated because of their small size.

English: a fool and his money are soon parted
meaning: It is difficult or unlikely that careless and irresponsible individuals will maintain their hold on acquired wealth.
Vietnamese: Kẻ dại thì tiền chẳng giữ được lâu
back-translation: A fool can't keep money long

meaning: People are drawn to others who have different or complementary traits, personalities, or characteristics.
Discharging one's obligations must take precedence over devoting time to pursuits meant solely for one's own gratification.
More can be accomplished by a team with a common goal than by individuals.

English: there's a sucker born every minute
meaning: There will always be a great number of fools in the world who can be easily swindled.
Vietnamese: Trên đời chẳng bao giờ thiếu kẻ cả tin dễ bị lừa
back-translation: The world never lacks gullible people who are easy to fool

English: the apple does not fall far from the tree
meaning: A child grows up to be similar to its parents, both in behavior and in physical characteristics.
Vietnamese: Con nhà tông không giống lông cũng giống cánh
back-translation: Like father, like son; children take after their family

meaning: The rules are certain and cannot be ignored or worked around.
Service staff should give high priority to customer satisfaction.
Used ironically to imply the opposite: Something has gone wrong.
Vietnamese: Lại thêm một ngày tuyệt vời ghê cơ

English: it takes two to make a quarrel
meaning: It takes two or more people to cause a quarrel; one cannot blame an argument entirely on the other side.
Vietnamese: Đã cãi nhau thì lỗi chẳng của riêng ai
back-translation: In a quarrel, the fault is never one side's alone

English: it takes a village to raise a child
meaning: An entire community of people must provide for, and interact positively with, children in order for those children to grow up healthily and safely.
Vietnamese: Nuôi dạy một đứa trẻ cần sự chung tay của cộng đồng
back-translation: Raising a child requires the community's joint help

meaning: If one practices an activity enough, one will steadily make progress and eventually be able to master it in time.
Vietnamese: Càng luyện tập càng tiến bộ
back-translation: The more you practice, the more you improve

meaning: The most important consideration in buying real estate is its location.
Vietnamese: Mua nhà đất, quan trọng nhất là vị trí
back-translation: When buying property, location matters most

meaning: Money or moneyed interests have power.
Vietnamese: Có tiền mua tiên cũng được
back-translation: Money can buy anything, even fairies; money talks

English: the devil is in the details
meaning: The specific provisions of, or particular steps for implementing, a general plan, policy, or contract may be complicated, controversial, or unworkable.
Vietnamese: Cái khó nằm ở những chi tiết
back-translation: The difficulty lies in the details

meaning: Commenting on a situation that has led to some unexpected outcome in a surprising or convoluted way.
back-translation: Heaven's will is hard to predict

meaning: Wealth cannot be obtained without some effort; hence currency is not always available for a prospective purchase.
A situation where the pressure that a person is under makes them demonstrate their potential.
Vietnamese: Lửa thử vàng, gian nan thử sức
back-translation: Fire tests gold, hardship tests strength

English: when the cat's away the mice will play
meaning: In the absence of a controlling entity, subordinates will take advantage of circumstances.
Vietnamese: Vắng chủ nhà, gà vọc niêu tôm
back-translation: When the cat's away, the mice will play

English: it ain't over 'til the fat lady sings
meaning: There are more developments yet to come; one should not presume to know the outcome of an event which is still in progress.
Vietnamese: Chưa đến phút cuối thì chưa biết thế nào
back-translation: Until the last minute, you never know how it will go

English: once a thief, always a thief
meaning: A person found to have stolen another's property will always be marked as a thief.
Vietnamese: Đã một lần ăn cắp thì mãi mang tiếng kẻ trộm
back-translation: Steal once and you're labeled a thief forever

English: a drowning man will clutch at a straw
meaning: A person in urgent need of assistance will seize any available form of aid, regardless of its insignificance.
Vietnamese: Sắp chết đuối thì cọng rơm cũng bám
back-translation: A drowning person will clutch at straws

English: there's no business like show business
meaning: The domain of the entertainment industry is more dazzling and exciting than any other business.
Vietnamese: Không nghề nào hào nhoáng như nghề giải trí
back-translation: No profession is as glamorous as the entertainment business

English: don't hate the player, hate the game
meaning: The frustrations with a system or activity should be blamed on its weaknesses, rather than on individuals who operate within it.
Vietnamese: Đừng trách người trong cuộc, hãy trách luật chơi
back-translation: Don't blame the players, blame the rules of the game

English: when one door closes, another opens
meaning: When one opportunity is lost, another opportunity soon becomes available.
back-translation: Heaven never shuts off every way out for people

meaning: A saying or advice suggesting to someone that instead of getting angry at a perceived injustice, slight or other action against them, they should retaliate.
Vietnamese: Đừng chỉ tức giận, hãy đáp trả cho đáng
example: She said that about you behind your back? Don't get mad, get even!
example Vietnamese: Cô ta nói xấu sau lưng bạn như thế à? Đừng chỉ tức giận, hãy đáp trả đi!
back-translation: Don't just get angry, respond in a way they deserve

meaning: Even small contributions towards a goal help bring the goal nearer.
Vietnamese: Góp gió thành bão, chút nào cũng quý
back-translation: Many small bits add up; every little bit is precious

English: love the sinner, hate the sin
meaning: One should not treat people badly because of their faults, but one should not go so far as to accept or approve the faults themselves.
Vietnamese: Ghét tội lỗi nhưng hãy thương người phạm lỗi
back-translation: Hate the sin but love the sinner

meaning: There is always a risk of being overheard, so one should be careful about what one says.

English: a trouble shared is a trouble halved
meaning: Talking about one's difficulties can alleviate one's worry and stress.
Vietnamese: Khó khăn được giãi bày sẽ nhẹ đi một nửa
back-translation: A trouble that is confided gets half lighter

English: a healthy body is a healthy mind
meaning: Physical fitness leads to mental acuity.
Vietnamese: Thân thể khỏe mạnh thì tinh thần minh mẫn
back-translation: A healthy body means a clear mind

meaning: Exploit any possible opportunity that arises from difficult situations.
Vietnamese: Đừng bỏ lỡ cơ hội mà khủng hoảng mang lại
back-translation: Don't miss the opportunity a crisis brings

English: one man's terrorist is another man's freedom fighter
meaning: one's view on war and political violence depends on perspective
Vietnamese: Kẻ bị bên này gọi là khủng bố lại là anh hùng của bên kia
back-translation: One side's terrorist is the other side's hero

English: play stupid games, win stupid prizes
meaning: If one makes poor decisions, then one should expect negative consequences.
Vietnamese: Chơi dại thì lãnh hậu quả
back-translation: Play foolishly and you suffer the consequences

meaning: An allusive shortening of lightning never strikes twice in the same place, usually used figuratively.
Vietnamese: Chuyện hiếm gặp khó mà xảy ra lần nữa
back-translation: A rare thing is unlikely to happen again

English: half a loaf is better than none
meaning: Something is better than nothing: some reward, achievement, result, etc. is preferable to none at all.
back-translation: A distorted thing is better than nothing

meaning: Personal health and wellbeing is determined by one's eating habits, in both positive and negative ways.
Vietnamese: Ăn uống thế nào thì sức khỏe thế ấy
back-translation: Your health is as your diet is

meaning: Advance awareness of a situation, especially a risky one, prepares one to deal with it.
Vietnamese: Biết trước thì phòng được trước
back-translation: Knowing in advance lets you guard in advance; forewarned is forearmed

English: you get what you pay for
meaning: In commercial transactions, the prices increase, as the quality of goods and services increases, i.e., the more one pays, the higher-quality the merchandise.
back-translation: You get what you pay for

English: he who laughs last laughs best
meaning: Success is enjoyed more after having previously endured ridicule.
Vietnamese: Cười người hôm trước, hôm sau người cười
back-translation: Laugh at others today, others will laugh at you tomorrow
check note: Warns mockers of payback; loses sweeter final success after enduring ridicule.

English: live by the sword, die by the sword
meaning: One who uses violence can expect a violent response; it is better to try to use peaceful means wherever possible.
Vietnamese: Chơi dao có ngày đứt tay
back-translation: Play with knives and one day you'll cut your hand
check note: Means risky behaviour backfires; violence provoking violent response is weakened.

meaning: People who are wicked must work harder than normal people.
Vietnamese: Số vất vả nên chẳng được nghỉ ngơi
back-translation: Fated to toil, so one gets no rest
check note: Drops wickedness; reads as a hard fate, not the wicked working harder.

English: a rising tide lifts all boats
meaning: A truly good outcome benefits all.
back-translation: When the water rises, the boat rises
check note: Suggests things rising with circumstances; benefit to everyone is not conveyed.

meaning: Different people like different things; there's no accounting for taste.
back-translation: Nine people, ten opinions; everyone thinks differently
check note: About differing opinions or disagreement rather than differing likes and tastes.

English: the captain goes down with the ship
meaning: A leader is ultimately responsible for the penalities of a catastrophe, even if they result from external causes or the misactions of others under the leader's purview.
Vietnamese: Người đứng đầu phải sống chết cùng con thuyền của mình
back-translation: The leader must live and die with their ship
check note: Stresses sharing the ship's fate; bearing ultimate responsibility for failure is only implied.

meaning: One is sure to succeed at a task or event on the third try.
Vietnamese: Quá tam ba bận, lần thứ ba ắt thành
back-translation: Third time is sure to succeed
check note: 'Quá tam ba bận' usually means a three-time limit; muddles the lucky-third sense.

meaning: The tactics or strategies of an adversary can also be used against them.
Vietnamese: Anh làm được thì tôi cũng làm được
back-translation: If you can do it, so can I
check note: Reads as matching ability; the retaliation-in-kind warning is weak.

meaning: To obtain the services of (a person) in exchange for remuneration; to give someone a job.
To spend free time out of the house.
example: You work too hard. You should get out more.
example Vietnamese: Bạn làm việc nhiều quá. Nên ra ngoài chơi nhiều hơn.
back-translation: get out of the house to unwind

meaning: To duck or take cover, usually to avoid harm. Commonly used as a caution or warning in the imperative.
example: With bullets flying, all I could do was get down and pray.
example Vietnamese: Đạn bay vèo vèo, tôi chỉ biết nằm rạp xuống và cầu nguyện.

meaning: To operate with a particular energy source.
example: This car runs on bio-alcohol.
example Vietnamese: Chiếc xe này chạy bằng cồn sinh học.

meaning: To delay the progress of, especially in school.
example: He's a year older than his classmates, because he was held back in second grade.
example Vietnamese: Cậu ấy lớn hơn bạn cùng lớp một tuổi vì bị lưu ban năm lớp hai.
back-translation: to make (a pupil) repeat a year

meaning: To leave; to set out; to begin a journey or trip.
example: He set off in search of better opportunities.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy lên đường tìm kiếm cơ hội tốt hơn.

meaning: To block something completely and physically.
example: The fat that I drained off the meat clogged up the drain.
example Vietnamese: Mỡ tôi chắt từ thịt ra đã làm tắc ống thoát nước.

meaning: To cease or stop.
example: The rain shows no sign of letting up.
example Vietnamese: Mưa chẳng có dấu hiệu gì là sẽ ngớt.

meaning: To disintegrate, to break into pieces.
example: My old briefcase is falling apart. I'll have to buy a new one.
example Vietnamese: Cái cặp cũ của tôi sắp rã ra rồi. Tôi phải mua cái mới.

meaning: To get through a difficult time; to overcome a source of grief.
Vietnamese: vượt qua giai đoạn đau buồn
back-translation: to get past a period of grief

meaning: Used to grant permission for or to give endorsement of a suggestion or proposal.
example: Go ahead and eat without me. I expect to be very late.
example Vietnamese: Cứ ăn trước đi, đừng đợi tôi. Chắc tôi sẽ về rất muộn.
back-translation: just go ahead and do it

meaning: To assume a sitting position from a position lying down.
example: Despite being cancer-ridden, Lorin sat up to greet the visitors.

meaning: To remain united, to stay together in association or alliance.
Vietnamese: đoàn kết gắn bó với nhau

meaning: To pull something out with a sudden jerk.
example: He suddenly whipped out his gun and pointed it at his doctor.
example Vietnamese: Hắn bất ngờ rút phắt súng ra chĩa vào bác sĩ của mình.

meaning: To succeed; to result in a satisfactory situation.
example: Are you still seeing John? - No, it didn't work out.
example Vietnamese: Bạn vẫn đang hẹn hò với John chứ? - Không, chuyện không thành.

meaning: To avoid or not go anywhere near someone or something.
example: The job could involve you staying away from home.
example Vietnamese: Công việc này có thể khiến bạn phải ở xa nhà.

meaning: To complete a form or questionnaire with requested information.
example: Please fill out this application if you are interested in the job.

meaning: To resume something previously cancelled or delayed; to continue something despite known concerns.
To reschedule (something) to an earlier date or time.
example: The meeting was moved up to Tuesday.
example Vietnamese: Cuộc họp đã được dời lên thứ Ba.
back-translation: to move to an earlier time

meaning: To hide.
example: The guerrillas holed up in a small cave.
example Vietnamese: Quân du kích ẩn náu trong một hang nhỏ.

meaning: To consume, deplete, expend, or exhaust.
To cause to fall to the floor
To exit a user account in a computer system, so that one is not recognized until signing in again.
example: Please don't forget to log out after you finish your work.

meaning: To enter a query into a database or search engine.
example: If you look up a bunch of random characters, there will probably be no results.
example Vietnamese: Nếu bạn tra một chuỗi ký tự ngẫu nhiên, chắc sẽ chẳng có kết quả nào.

meaning: To participate, take part or get involved in something.
To reschedule (something) to a later date or time.
Vietnamese: dời lại sang lúc muộn hơn
example: The report still hasn't been completed, so the meeting will have to be moved back again.
example Vietnamese: Báo cáo vẫn chưa xong nên cuộc họp lại phải lùi lịch.
back-translation: to postpone to a later time

meaning: To act as a replacement or substitute.
back-translation: to step in and do it in someone's place

meaning: To log in ("gain access, usually by providing a previously registered username and password") to (a computer system).
To manage to produce, deliver, or present (something) by inventing, creating, thinking of, or obtaining it.
example: How can you come up with such brilliant ideas?
example Vietnamese: Làm sao bạn nghĩ ra được những ý tưởng tuyệt vời như vậy?

meaning: To enter suddenly or unexpectedly while something is happening; to intrude or interrupt by entering.
Vietnamese: bất ngờ bước vào bắt gặp
example: He accidentally walked in on me while I was undressing.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy vô tình bước vào đúng lúc tôi đang cởi đồ.
back-translation: to unexpectedly walk in and catch

meaning: To select (someone or something) from a group and highlight them or treat them differently.
example: Eddie singled out his favorite marble from the bag.
example Vietnamese: Eddie chọn riêng viên bi mình thích nhất trong túi.

meaning: To escape, especially forcefully or defiantly.
Vietnamese: phá vòng giam để trốn thoát
example: They broke out of prison in the middle of the night.
example Vietnamese: Họ vượt ngục giữa đêm khuya.
back-translation: break out of confinement to escape

meaning: To subsist; to succeed, survive, or manage, at least at a minimal level.
example: Do you think they can get by on only one salary?

meaning: To opt out of conventional society.
Vietnamese: sống tách khỏi nếp xã hội thông thường
back-translation: to live apart from conventional social ways

meaning: To engage in playful fun.
example: I think he was just kidding around when he said that, so don't take it personally.
example Vietnamese: Tôi nghĩ lúc nói vậy anh ấy chỉ đùa thôi, đừng để bụng.

meaning: To transfer (property or rights) to somebody else by signing a document.
example: He signed his house over to his wife in order to avoid taxes.
example Vietnamese: Ông ấy ký chuyển nhượng căn nhà cho vợ để tránh thuế.

meaning: To do something in a manner that lacks seriousness, commitment, or professionalism.
Vietnamese: làm kiểu chơi chơi, thiếu nghiêm túc
back-translation: to do something playfully, not seriously

meaning: To engage in a formal or informal process.
example: The country entered into peace talks with the militants.
example Vietnamese: Nước này đã bước vào đàm phán hòa bình với phiến quân.

meaning: To introduce, add or initiate a person or group of people to an organisation or event; to give (someone) a share or portion of something.
Vietnamese: đưa người mới vào tham gia
back-translation: to bring a new person in to participate

meaning: To deeply enjoy or be fulfilled by something esteemed as very important in one's life.
example: I live for knowledge.
example Vietnamese: Tôi sống vì tri thức.
back-translation: to regard as one's reason for living

meaning: To play truant
example: We all bunked off school yesterday to watch the football.
example Vietnamese: Hôm qua cả bọn tôi trốn học đi xem bóng đá.

meaning: To cause (something or someone) to become.
example: He turned water into wine.
example Vietnamese: Ông ấy biến nước thành rượu.

meaning: To walk with no planned destination; to meander.
To act in a way most suitable to; to act in a way that best brings out (a quality, condition, etc.).
example: He played to his strengths tonight.
example Vietnamese: Tối nay anh ấy đã phát huy đúng sở trường của mình.
back-translation: to make full use of one's strengths

meaning: To lead or direct someone to an enclosed space, usually a room.
example: I'll be in the library. When my guests arrive, show them in, Charlie.
example Vietnamese: Tôi sẽ ở trong thư viện. Khi khách đến, dẫn họ vào nhé, Charlie.

meaning: To close with a zip fastener.
example: Always check if you've zipped up your fly before you go out.
example Vietnamese: Trước khi ra ngoài, nhớ kiểm tra xem đã kéo khóa quần chưa.

meaning: To fix problems and difficult situations that (somebody) has continuously gotten themselves into.
Vietnamese: đi giải quyết hậu quả cho ai
back-translation: to go around dealing with the consequences for someone

meaning: To be so excited that one is no longer in control of one's actions or behavior.
To get away, or escape, taking (something) with one.
example: The thieves got away with a million pounds' worth of jewellery.
example Vietnamese: Bọn trộm cuỗm đi số nữ trang trị giá một triệu bảng.

meaning: To start dealing with something else.
example: The best revenge is always to just happily move on and let karma do the rest.
example Vietnamese: Cách trả thù hay nhất luôn là vui vẻ bước tiếp và để nghiệp quả lo phần còn lại.

meaning: To rely on, trust, or expect.
example: Don't count on being able to get back into the building after 5pm.
check note: Means await or hope for; loses the rely-on and trust sense.

meaning: To begin clanging or making noise.
example: The alarm will go off at six a.m.
check note: Bare 'kêu' is ambiguous; misses an alarm starting to ring.

meaning: To move into (an object), such that one ends up inside it.
example: She got into the car.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy lên xe.
check note: 'Chui' implies crawling or squeezing in, narrower than get into.

meaning: To come to a final place, condition, or situation, sometimes unplanned or unexpected; to turn out.
example: They ended up angry at each other.
example Vietnamese: Rốt cuộc họ lại giận nhau.
check note: Example 'lại giận nhau' can read as angry again.

meaning: To enter illegally or by force, especially in order to commit a crime.
example: Somebody broke into his car and stole his tools and CDs.
example Vietnamese: Kẻ nào đó đã phá xe anh ấy, lấy trộm đồ nghề và đĩa CD.
check note: Example 'phá xe' reads as wrecking the car, not breaking in.

meaning: To return, restore (a thing to its original owner or location etc.).
example: Give me back my book!
check note: Bare 'trả' also means pay; 'trả lại' is needed for clarity.

meaning: To suddenly start doing or producing something.
check note: Reads as something popping out; misses suddenly starting to do something.

meaning: To resemble (a parent or ancestor) in appearance or habit.
example: She takes after her grandmother with her wide eyes and quiet disposition.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy giống bà ở đôi mắt to và tính trầm lặng.
back-translation: resemble an adult in the family
check note: 'Adults in the household' is looser than parent or ancestor.

meaning: To diss; to put down.
example: Hey! Quit messing with my brother.
example Vietnamese: Này! Đừng có kiếm chuyện với em tao nữa.
back-translation: to look for trouble and pester
check note: Meaning is insult or put down; Vietnamese says provoke and pester.

meaning: To reply impertinently or rudely; to answer in a cheeky or rude manner.
example: Jane talked back a little too often.
example Vietnamese: Jane cãi lại hơi bị thường xuyên.
check note: Example's slang 'hơi bị' means 'quite often', losing 'too often'.

meaning: To be determined to do or achieve something.
example: I had my mind pretty well set on working for a small company.
example Vietnamese: Tôi đã gần như quyết chí làm cho một công ty nhỏ.
back-translation: to be determined to achieve something
check note: Example 'gần như quyết chí làm cho' is unnatural and ambiguous.

meaning: To lead or take the lead in; to direct; to take charge of.
example: We want you to head up the effort to organize all the entries.
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi muốn bạn phụ trách việc sắp xếp toàn bộ các mục gửi về.
back-translation: to head and be in charge of
check note: Example's 'các mục gửi về' is unnatural, unclear for competition entries.

meaning: To log off; to stop using a computer, radio, etc.; especially, to stop talking.
example: He finished the conversation and signed off.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy kết thúc cuộc trò chuyện rồi thoát ra.
check note: Headword phrase 'chào kết thúc' is unnatural and unclear Vietnamese.

meaning: To restrain; to check.
example: Please hold the noise down.
example Vietnamese: Làm ơn giữ yên lặng bớt đi.
check note: Example 'giữ yên lặng bớt đi' is unnatural; should say reduce the noise.

meaning: To put on some clothes rapidly.
check note: Says change outfits quickly; meaning is quickly put clothes on.

meaning: To dawdle, lollygag; to waste time aimlessly or engage in idle activity or inactivity.
example: He sat there goofing off all day instead of working.
example Vietnamese: Nó ngồi đó chơi bời cả ngày thay vì làm việc.
check note: Example's 'chơi bời' suggests carousing or loose living, not idling.

meaning: To get past a difficult or stressful situation by thinking or talking about it.
Vietnamese: trải lòng để vượt qua chuyện khó khăn
back-translation: to open one's heart to get through a difficulty
check note: 'Trải lòng' means confiding only; omits thinking the problem through.

meaning: To slowly move away from a point, especially if on water.
example: Watch the seafoam drift away from your feet.
example Vietnamese: Hãy ngắm bọt biển trôi dạt khỏi chân bạn.
check note: Example's 'bọt biển' commonly reads as sponge; seafoam is 'bọt sóng'.

meaning: To read, examine or engage in (something) in a cursory or casual manner.
example: Dip into a nice book.
example Vietnamese: Hãy nhẩn nha đọc một cuốn sách hay.
check note: Example says read leisurely; loses the casual dipping-in sense.

meaning: To notice (something) and comment on it; to recognize that (something) is important or novel enough to comment on it; to make a remark on (something).
example: He remarked on how good you are at the game.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy có nhận xét là bạn chơi trò này giỏi thế nào.
check note: Example 'có nhận xét là ... giỏi thế nào' is unnatural Vietnamese.

meaning: To affect the emotions of (a person) suddenly and overwhelmingly.
example: Embarrassment washed over me as I realized I had forgotten the notes for my presentation.
example Vietnamese: Nỗi xấu hổ trào lên trong tôi khi nhận ra mình đã quên ghi chú cho bài thuyết trình.
check note: Example reads as forgot to make notes, not forgot to bring them.

meaning: Especially in the form to hang about with (someone): to spend time or be friends with.
example: My daughter likes to hang about with older kids after school.
example Vietnamese: Con gái tôi thích la cà với bọn lớn tuổi hơn sau giờ học.
check note: Pejorative register (loafing, running with a crowd); English is neutral.

meaning: To be correct about what one says or thinks.
example: I knew I was in the right about John being older than his wife, despite looking younger.
example Vietnamese: Tôi biết mình đúng khi nói John lớn tuổi hơn vợ, dù trông anh ấy trẻ hơn.
back-translation: be the one who is right

meaning: Offered for sale.
Used as a rhetorical question to confirm agreement, knowing or understanding at the end of a statement.
example: But I guess that's life, you know?
example Vietnamese: Nhưng chắc đời là thế, bạn hiểu mà?

meaning: Relating to a relatively short period of time.
Implies that a statement is based on a guess or assumption rather than on knowledge or evidence.
Vietnamese: mà tôi thì biết gì đâu
example: Maybe girl grasshoppers find long legs attractive in boy grasshoppers, but what do I know?
example Vietnamese: Có lẽ châu chấu cái thấy mấy chàng châu chấu chân dài là hấp dẫn, mà tôi thì biết gì đâu?

meaning: Indicating that one is overwhelmed with a situation, due to it being extremely hilarious, emotional, frustrating, etc.
back-translation: I can't take it any more

meaning: A polite request for information.
example: I'd like to know more about the graduate admissions process.
example Vietnamese: Tôi muốn biết thêm về quy trình tuyển sinh sau đại học.

meaning: To a certain degree; to an extent; in a certain sense.
In waiting; in readiness.
example: He's got some bad news in store for us, judging from his mood.
example Vietnamese: Nhìn tâm trạng ông ấy thì chắc đang có tin xấu chờ chúng ta.

meaning: Used to indicate indifference, often as a reply to an unimportant or irrelevant statement.
example: I lost my red shoes. - So what? Get a new pair.

meaning: An affirmative reply; yes; certainly.
example: "Can you finish by tomorrow?" / "Sure thing!"
example Vietnamese: "Mai cậu làm xong được không?" / "Chắc chắn rồi!"

meaning: Used to say that something is too strange, embarrassing, or complicated to explain.
An exclamation or expression of alarm about a problem or error.
example: Oh, no! The rug is on fire!
example Vietnamese: Ôi không! Tấm thảm cháy rồi!

meaning: exactly
Said to someone coming back to their own home.
I intend no offense by these remarks.
Vietnamese: không có ý xúc phạm đâu

meaning: Seemingly new; as good as new.
example: After a thorough shine, your shoes look like new.
example Vietnamese: Đánh bóng kỹ xong, đôi giày của bạn trông như mới.

meaning: Expressing hope that the listener will soon recover from illness.
Said when something is starting to happen.
By appearance.
Used to acknowledge or invite reflection about an event (sometimes facetiously).
Requiring little effort or sacrifice on your part, with the implication that it is or has been more difficult for others.
Used to propose marriage to someone
Undecided; wavering in one's opinion.
example: I am still on the fence about which way to vote.
example Vietnamese: Tôi vẫn đang phân vân không biết nên bỏ phiếu cho bên nào.

meaning: Having a streak of good luck or good progress or success.
example: He was on a roll with the answers that day and didn't want to stop.
example Vietnamese: Hôm đó anh ấy đang đà trả lời hay và không muốn dừng lại.
back-translation: on a winning streak, riding toward victory

meaning: Used to ask a stranger asking a question to identify themselves
example: "Are you the owner of this vehicle?" / "Who's asking?"
example Vietnamese: "Anh là chủ chiếc xe này à?" / "Ai hỏi đấy?"

meaning: On a level; in the same condition, circumstances, position, rank, etc.; equal.
example: Their pretensions are on a par.

meaning: Used to introduce a question, implying that eliciting an affirmative answer from the interlocutor would be unlikely yet desirable for the speaker.
example: I don't suppose you could show me the way to the museum?
example Vietnamese: Không biết liệu anh có thể chỉ cho tôi đường đến bảo tàng không?
back-translation: I wonder if it would be possible

meaning: With such a purpose as.
Used as a positive response of affirmation towards a male subordinate.
If (something) were not (or had not been) there; in the absence of (something); without.
example: If not for her surgical skill, you'd be dead now, so some appreciation may be in order.
example Vietnamese: Nếu không nhờ tay nghề phẫu thuật của cô ấy thì giờ anh đã chết, nên biết ơn một chút đi.

meaning: Used before stating something that the speaker believes to be correct
Into two halves.
example: I broke the brank in half.
example Vietnamese: Tôi bẻ cành cây làm đôi.

meaning: I informally request that you kiss me-that you touch my lips with your lips or press the lips against, as an expression of love or affection.
back-translation: kiss me (said to a lover by female / to 'em')

meaning: A reply indicating uncaring.
Calling for other people to say something together.
Vietnamese: mọi người cùng đồng thanh nào
example: All together! Say it: "Long live our country!"
example Vietnamese: Cùng đồng thanh nào! Hô lên: "Đất nước muôn năm!"

meaning: In aggressive pursuit; searching relentlessly.
example: Police are on the hunt for the suspect.
example Vietnamese: Cảnh sát đang ráo riết truy tìm nghi phạm.

meaning: At this moment; right now.
example: I'm really off horror movies at the moment.

meaning: good-bye

English: do you have any brothers or sisters
meaning: Used to ask whether someone has any siblings.
Vietnamese: Nhà bạn có anh chị em gì không?
back-translation: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

meaning: I believe that is the case, but am not certain.
Possessing similar or identical qualities.
example: I hate being alone with my boss as we have nothing in common.
example Vietnamese: Tôi ghét ở riêng với sếp vì chúng tôi chẳng có gì chung.

meaning: Expressing disapproval of or encouraging actions against a person, organization, practice, belief, etc., typically in a public protest.
example: Down with the government!

meaning: Ringing the doorbell or knocking on the door.
example: That would be Mom at the door.
example Vietnamese: Chắc là mẹ đang ở ngoài cửa.

meaning: Used to indicate that a specified or implied action cannot succeed or offers no advantage if successful
example: What's the use trying to tell him? He won't listen.
example Vietnamese: Nói với anh ta thì có ích gì? Anh ta đâu chịu nghe.

meaning: Used to express when someone or something has saved the day, or provided valuable help.
Saying used to encourage someone to keep moving despite hardship
apparently, outwardly; superficially
back-translation: on the surface, judging by appearances

meaning: It is only known to God; it is unknown to people.
example: Don't touch that! God knows who else put their hands on that thing!
example Vietnamese: Đừng đụng vào đó! Có trời mới biết còn ai đã sờ tay vào thứ ấy!

meaning: Beneath the surface; in the internal workings.
example: Internet search engines are easy to use, but there's a lot going on under the hood.
example Vietnamese: Công cụ tìm kiếm trên mạng thì dễ dùng, nhưng bên trong có rất nhiều thứ đang vận hành.

meaning: A response used to indicate that speaker was in agreement with the preceding statement before it was made.
check note: Reads as 'I knew it/I already know', weak as agreement.

meaning: I don't know.
back-translation: nothing to be done / I give up
check note: Also reads as 'can't be helped'; 'I don't know' not explicit.

meaning: An affirmation of romantic feeling to a lover or spouse.
check note: Fixes speaker as woman addressing a man only.

meaning: In the position ahead. Often with of.
example: The leader, Jones, is well in front.
example Vietnamese: Người dẫn đầu, Jones, đang bỏ xa phía trước.
check note: Example phrasing 'bỏ xa phía trước' is unnatural, lacks proper object.

meaning: Working, in the process of doing work.
example: Don't interrupt me while I'm at work on my housing project.
example Vietnamese: Đừng ngắt lời khi tôi đang làm dự án nhà ở.
check note: Example 'ngắt lời' means interrupting speech, not interrupting someone working.

meaning: Simultaneously at each occurrence (of some action).
check note: Reads as 'every time'; simultaneous-per-occurrence sense unclear without quantity.

meaning: Insufficiently equipped with.
example: He's a nice person, but a bit short of brains.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy tốt tính, nhưng đầu óc hơi thiếu hụt.
check note: Example 'đầu óc hơi thiếu hụt' is unnatural Vietnamese.

meaning: Fully; to the whole extent.
example: My creditors insist on being repaid in full before the end of the month.
example Vietnamese: Các chủ nợ nhất quyết đòi tôi trả đủ trước cuối tháng.
check note: Headword rendering 'đầy đủ toàn bộ' is redundant and unnatural.

meaning: A greeting or farewell said in the afternoon.
example: Good afternoon everyone and thank you for coming to our special meeting today.
example Vietnamese: Chào mọi người, cảm ơn đã đến dự buổi họp đặc biệt hôm nay.
check note: Example drops 'good afternoon'; greeting becomes a generic hello.

meaning: Prior to an expected or scheduled time; early.
example: He navigated the course adeptly, having trained on it for months ahead of time.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy lái qua đường đua thuần thục vì đã tập trên đó trước hàng tháng trời.
back-translation: ahead of the deadline, in advance
check note: Example adds driving on a racetrack; source only says navigated the course.

meaning: Unavailable because the stock in inventory has all been sold or used up.
example: The turkeys are out of stock but we have some guinea fowl in the back.
example Vietnamese: Gà tây hết hàng rồi, nhưng phía sau chúng tôi còn ít gà sao.
check note: Example 'phía sau chúng tôi' reads as 'behind us', not stockroom.

meaning: In the most favorable of conditions, especially in a situation that is otherwise negative.
check note: 'Cùng lắm thì' also reads as 'at worst'; best-case sense unclear.

meaning: Expresses disbelief.
example: Your dog ate your homework? Yeah, right.
example Vietnamese: Chó ăn mất bài tập của em á? Ừ, tin được chắc.
back-translation: Yeah, sure I believe that (sarcastic or sincere)
check note: Sarcasm unclear in writing; may read as sincere belief.

meaning: Used to introduce a rebuttal to the interlocutor's previous statement, especially when the statement angered or offended the speaker.
example: For your information, my son was a straight A student in college, so he's not just some schmo!
example Vietnamese: Nói cho mà biết, con trai tôi là sinh viên toàn điểm A ở đại học, nó đâu phải hạng xoàng!
back-translation: just so you know, let me tell you
check note: Example implies son is still a student; source says was.

meaning: Used to express hopes that someone does well in an endeavor.
back-translation: Wishing you the best of luck
check note: Unnatural calque; usual wish is 'Chúc bạn gặp nhiều may mắn'.

meaning: An informal greeting.
check note: Final 'nhé' makes it sound like a goodbye rather than a greeting.

meaning: Used as an intensifier to emphasize typicality of behavior
Vietnamese: đúng là kiểu của người ta
example: That's Jane for you, always moaning about something.
example Vietnamese: Jane là thế đấy, lúc nào cũng than vãn chuyện gì đó.
back-translation: that's just typical of that person
check note: Headword 'của người ta' is awkward and vague; reads as 'people's way'.

meaning: What a surprise; guess what.
example: Well, what do you know, it's raining again.
check note: 'ai dè' is a clause connector, unnatural as a standalone exclamation.

meaning: Observes, with (sometimes ironic) surprise, that a specified thing or person is present.
example: Why, if it isn't Bill! Come on in, Bill!
example Vietnamese: Ôi, ai như Bill thế này! Vào đi, Bill!
check note: Headword lacks a name slot; alone reads like 'who is like this'.

meaning: as to show disagreement, opposition or disapproval.
example: We set that up in protest of the government's actions.
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi lập ra việc đó để phản đối các hành động của chính phủ.
check note: Example's 'lập ra việc đó' is unnatural, unclear for 'set that up'.

meaning: Available to be summoned.
Vietnamese: trực sẵn, gọi là có mặt
example: He spent the weekend on call and couldn't fully relax.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy trực gọi suốt cuối tuần nên không thể thư giãn hẳn.
check note: Example's 'trực gọi' is an unnatural calque for being on call.

meaning: In correct proportion relative to other objects, contexts, etc.
Vietnamese: đúng với tầm mức thực của nó
example: I'm having trouble trying to keep things in perspective right now.
example Vietnamese: Lúc này tôi đang khó mà nhìn mọi việc cho đúng mực.
back-translation: at its true scale / in proportion
check note: Example's "đúng mực" suggests proper/decorous, not in proportion.

meaning: To learn to play (an instrument) or sing by listening to recorded music without reading or memorizing sheet music or without any formal instruction.
Vietnamese: chơi nhạc bằng cách nghe, không cần bản nhạc
back-translation: play music by ear, without sheet music
check note: Covers only playing; omits learning and singing.

meaning: To agree or be pleased (with something).
check note: Direction differs: thing being accepted, not someone agreeing or pleased.

meaning: In large amounts or numbers.
example: It's not available in sufficient quantity.
example Vietnamese: Thứ này không có đủ số lượng.
check note: Example is unnatural and drops the sense of availability.

meaning: A stand-in for trivial, obvious, or boring content.
check note: Describes loud, careless chatter; not a filler for trivial or boring content.

meaning: Used as part of greeting of two people who have not been in contact for a long time.
Said to someone before they fall asleep, wishing them a good sleep.
Vietnamese: Chúc ngủ ngon và mơ đẹp

meaning: To have an adventurous or perilous lifestyle; to behave in a manner which creates risks for oneself.
Vietnamese: sống liều lĩnh, thích mạo hiểm

meaning: A place or part of a place, especially one that is small, remote, or tedious to access.
example: Everyone helped out to clean every nook and cranny of the house.
example Vietnamese: Mọi người cùng chung tay dọn sạch từng ngóc ngách trong nhà.

meaning: A mystery; something unknown or unpredictable.
To work studiously, especially late into the night.
Vietnamese: thức khuya miệt mài làm việc
example: He was burning the midnight oil to finish his paper.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy thức khuya miệt mài để hoàn thành bài viết.
back-translation: to stay up late working hard

meaning: Used to shift focus to an overriding point or impediment.
example: I'd like to come, but the thing is, I just can't afford it.
example Vietnamese: Tôi muốn đến lắm, nhưng vấn đề là tôi không đủ tiền.

meaning: To not care at all; to have no interest or concern; to be apathetic.
Physically unfit.
Used to express reluctance, to express that if one hypothetical or possible action happened, it would not make any notable difference.
Vietnamese: đằng nào cũng vậy thì cứ
back-translation: since it makes no difference, might as well

meaning: To enjoy oneself.
back-translation: have fun to your heart's content

meaning: Watching alertly or attentively.
back-translation: to watch intently, follow with one's eyes

meaning: used to add emphasis to "why" in a question.
example: Why in the world would you spend so much money on a toy?
example Vietnamese: Sao bạn lại đi tốn ngần ấy tiền cho một món đồ chơi chứ?

English: take a turn for the better
meaning: To start to become better; to improve.
Not incarcerated or in captivity; not under control.
My fault; mea culpa.
example: Yes, I realise the car isn't supposed to be parked in the heirloom flowerbed. My bad.
example Vietnamese: Vâng, tôi biết không được đỗ xe trong luống hoa quý. Lỗi của tôi.

meaning: right now, or in the near and foreseeable future
To reach a negotiated agreement.
Up to the present.
example: As yet, we have not received the letter you sent us.
example Vietnamese: Đến nay, chúng tôi vẫn chưa nhận được thư anh gửi.

meaning: From nowhere or nothing; from a non-existent or unknown source.
example: They don't seem to want to work to earn a living. They think they can make money out of thin air.
example Vietnamese: Họ có vẻ không muốn làm việc kiếm sống. Họ tưởng tiền tự trên trời rơi xuống.

meaning: The wrong crowd.
Compensation for injury caused by a person, in the form of inflicting an identical injury on that person.
Vietnamese: mắt đền mắt, răng đền răng
back-translation: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth

meaning: In need of refinement; unsophisticated.
Vietnamese: còn thô ráp, chưa được trau chuốt
example: While rough around the edges, the church is really a wonderful place to be.
example Vietnamese: Tuy còn mộc mạc thô ráp, nhà thờ thật sự là một nơi tuyệt vời để đến.

meaning: Honest(ly), sincere(ly), straightforward(ly), fair(ly).
example: He looks like a used car salesman, but he's really on the level, so you can trust him.
example Vietnamese: Trông anh ta như dân bán xe cũ, nhưng thật ra rất đàng hoàng, nên bạn có thể tin.

meaning: Used to express one's defiance.
Vietnamese: Thế đấy, làm gì được nào
back-translation: That's how it is, what can you do about it

meaning: After a long time; eventually.
example: Now that the dog has stopped barking, perhaps we can at last get some rest.
example Vietnamese: Giờ con chó đã thôi sủa, có lẽ cuối cùng chúng ta cũng được nghỉ ngơi.

meaning: A heated, angry, or confused atmosphere calms down.
example: I tried to make amends after the dust settled.
example Vietnamese: Tôi tìm cách làm hòa sau khi mọi chuyện đã lắng xuống.

meaning: To make a mistake, a bad decision or act senselessly and get into an extremely difficult situation.
To have everything one needs.
Emphasises the truth of a statement.
example: We had trouble getting that grand piano up the stairs, I can tell you!
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi vất vả lắm mới đưa được cây đại dương cầm đó lên cầu thang, nói thật đấy!

meaning: Very poor, to the point of starving or begging; utterly destitute.
Of exceptionally high quality; wonderful; marvelous; excellent.
Vietnamese: tuyệt vời không chê vào đâu được
example: You must try the chef's special: it's just out of this world.
example Vietnamese: Bạn phải thử món đặc biệt của bếp trưởng: ngon tuyệt cú mèo.

meaning: Used to suggest an understatement.
Vietnamese: ấy là còn nói nhẹ đi
example: The 9/11 attacks weren't very good for America. / To say the least!
example Vietnamese: Vụ tấn công 11/9 chẳng tốt đẹp gì cho nước Mỹ. / Nói thế còn là nhẹ đấy!

meaning: To fail in one's responsibilities or duties, or to make a mistake, especially at a critical point or when the result is very negative.
back-translation: be careless and let things go wrong

meaning: To ignore.
example: He took no notice of the spider until it bit him.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy chẳng để ý đến con nhện cho đến khi bị nó cắn.
back-translation: to not bother paying attention to

meaning: Contrary to what is expected; especially, of behavior different from what society expects.
A period of peace before a disturbance or crisis; an unnatural or false calm before a storm.
example: The meeting may be peaceful now, but this is only the calm before the storm.

meaning: Regularly; occurring in regular time intervals or patterns.
A large amount of activity and work, usually in a noisy surrounding.
example: He moved to his parents' farm to have a break from the hustle and bustle of the big city.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy chuyển về trang trại của bố mẹ để tạm rời xa sự hối hả, ồn ào của thành phố lớn.

meaning: To separate from someone or something.
example: If we can't agree on whether to have children, maybe it's time to say goodbye.
example Vietnamese: Nếu không thống nhất được chuyện có con hay không, có lẽ đã đến lúc chia tay.

meaning: Of parents not legally married.
example: Some children are born out of wedlock.
example Vietnamese: Một số đứa trẻ được sinh ra ngoài giá thú.

meaning: To infer a meaning that is not stated explicitly.
example: If you read between the lines a little, you will realize that he has deeper motives.
example Vietnamese: Nếu chịu đọc ra ẩn ý một chút, bạn sẽ nhận ra anh ta có động cơ sâu xa hơn.

meaning: Writings, objects, or knowledge from the past that no longer exist.
example: The enormous collection of manuscripts from the Library of Alexandria is lost to history.
example Vietnamese: Kho bản thảo đồ sộ của Thư viện Alexandria đã thất truyền.
back-translation: lost to posterity (no longer handed down)

meaning: In disagreement; conflicting.
example: The witness's statement seems to be at odds with the evidence-not a good sign for the prosecutor.
example Vietnamese: Lời khai của nhân chứng có vẻ mâu thuẫn với bằng chứng, điềm chẳng lành cho công tố viên.

meaning: To correct a previous error or misunderstanding, especially one in print.
back-translation: issue a correction / set the record straight

meaning: To have achieved a lifestyle characterized by good fortune and comfort.
Vietnamese: được sống sung túc, an nhàn
example: It's a great idea, and if it catches on and sells well, we'll have it made.
example Vietnamese: Đó là ý tưởng tuyệt vời, nếu nó được ưa chuộng và bán chạy thì chúng ta sẽ đổi đời.
back-translation: to live in comfort and ease

meaning: Indicating acceptance, often with resignation or acquiescence, of a statement or situation.
example: "Jeeves, fetch the wine from the cellar." "Very well, sir."
example Vietnamese: "Jeeves, xuống hầm lấy rượu lên." "Vâng, thưa ngài."

meaning: To accept praise, as performers in a theater at the end of their act.
Vietnamese: cúi chào nhận lời tán thưởng

meaning: At last.
To go from a standing position to a sitting one.
back-translation: to sit down and rest one's feet

meaning: In addition; also.
example: Wearing his hat and coat, he looked outside and decided he should take an umbrella as well.
example Vietnamese: Đội mũ, mặc áo khoác xong, anh nhìn ra ngoài và quyết định nên mang theo cả ô nữa.
check note: Headword rendering "cũng thế nữa" is unnatural, suggests "likewise".

meaning: To worsen; to fail or go amiss; to have a bad outcome.
example: Everything seems to be going very badly wrong today.
example Vietnamese: Hôm nay mọi thứ dường như đều trục trặc hết sức tệ hại.
check note: Awkward collocations, especially 'trục trặc hết sức tệ hại' in the example.

meaning: Depending upon some condition or requirement; provided that; if, assuming; as long as.
example: I don't mind if he stays there, so long as he cleans up after himself when he's done.
back-translation: exempt / as long as / free of (ambiguous single word 'mien')
check note: Bare 'miễn' is ambiguous (exempt); 'miễn là' is clearer.

meaning: Said to someone who has just sneezed, as a polite remark.
check note: Reads as farewell or toast health wish; not clearly a sneeze response.

meaning: An activity or domain in which someone is interested or skilled in; one's personal preference.
check note: 'Sở thích hợp gu' is redundant and unnatural.

meaning: To take care in doing something; to pay attention or ensure that something is done.
Vietnamese: chú tâm làm cho bằng được
example: My wallet is missing! I know I had it earlier: I made a point of bringing it.
example Vietnamese: Ví của tôi mất rồi! Rõ ràng lúc nãy còn: tôi đã cố ý mang theo mà.
back-translation: focus on making sure to do it
check note: 'Cho bằng được' implies determination at all costs, stronger than taking care.

meaning: To settle a dispute or disagreement.
example: The committee made peace and agreed to go with the new plan.
example Vietnamese: Ủy ban đã dàn hòa và đồng ý theo kế hoạch mới.
check note: Example 'dàn hòa' suggests mediating others' quarrel, not settling own dispute.

meaning: Upon cursory examination.
example: This report is certainly not comprehensive; it is more of a "Marketing Division at a glance".
example Vietnamese: Báo cáo này chắc chắn chưa đầy đủ; nó giống bản nhìn lướt về Phòng Tiếp thị hơn.
check note: Example phrase 'bản nhìn lướt' is unnatural Vietnamese for an overview.

meaning: To remove plates, etc. from a table after a meal.
back-translation: clear the dining table / set up the meal table (ambiguous: clear the table)
check note: 'Dọn bàn ăn' can also mean setting the table; direction ambiguous.

meaning: To conceive one's first child
Vietnamese: bắt đầu sinh con đầu lòng
check note: 'Bắt đầu sinh' is unnatural and means giving birth rather than conceiving.

meaning: To assume a clear and complete form when separate elements come together; to be fully realized at last.
example: If it weren't for your heroic deed, his evil plan would have fallen into place.
example Vietnamese: Nếu không nhờ hành động anh hùng của bạn, âm mưu của hắn đã trót lọt đâu vào đấy.
check note: Example's 'trót lọt đâu vào đấy' is an unnatural collocation.

meaning: To disturb the status quo or go against rules or conventions, as in an effort to get attention.
example: I'd just jump in and fix it, but that's not my job, and I don't want to rock the boat.
example Vietnamese: Tôi muốn nhảy vào sửa luôn, nhưng đó không phải việc của tôi, và tôi không muốn gây rắc rối.
back-translation: stir up the peace, disturb the calm
check note: 'Khuấy đảo sự yên ổn' is unnatural; 'khuấy đảo' suggests making a splash.

meaning: Greatly enjoys; likes a lot.
example: We'll need to bake more of those new chicken and mushroom pies. The customers can't get enough.
example Vietnamese: Ta cần nướng thêm bánh nhân gà nấm loại mới. Khách ăn mãi không chán.
back-translation: be absorbed and never tire of it
check note: 'Mê mãi' reads like misspelt 'mê mải'; headword phrase sounds unnatural.

meaning: Up to this point, all is OK.
check note: Omits 'so far / up to now', the core of the expression.

meaning: Any assistance, help or aid.
example: Thanks for lending a helping hand to the project.
example Vietnamese: Cảm ơn bạn đã giúp một tay cho dự án.
check note: 'Sự giúp một tay' is an unnatural nominalization.

meaning: Concede to mounting evidence; wake up and smell the coffee.
back-translation: take the hint and act accordingly
check note: Means catching a hint and complying; misses conceding to mounting evidence.

meaning: To confront or deal with directly; to commence a confrontation.
Vietnamese: đối mặt và chấp nhận giải quyết
example: Until she comes to grips with her mother's death, she has no hope of putting it behind her.
example Vietnamese: Chừng nào chưa đối mặt được với cái chết của mẹ, cô ấy không thể nào vượt qua nó.
check note: Headword 'chấp nhận giải quyết' is awkward, reads as 'agree to settle'.

meaning: Very soon.
Vietnamese: sắp đến nơi rồi, bất cứ lúc nào
example: The train will be arriving any time now.
example Vietnamese: Tàu sắp đến bất cứ lúc nào.
check note: Headword tied to arriving; 'sắp ... bất cứ lúc nào' is unnatural.

meaning: A movement from one location to another.
Vietnamese: sự thay đổi không khí, đổi chỗ ở
back-translation: a change of air, change of living place
check note: 'Đổi chỗ ở' implies moving house, narrower than changing location.

meaning: An expression used to convey mild self-deprecation or to acknowledge a mistake or oversight.
example: Oh, silly me! I forgot to buy the apples!
example Vietnamese: Ôi, mình ngớ ngẩn thật! Quên mua táo rồi!
check note: 'Đãng trí' limits it to forgetfulness, not general silly mistakes.

meaning: The past performance of a person, organization, or product, viewed in its entirety and usually for the purpose of making a judgment.
back-translation: past achievements / track record of successes
check note: 'Thành tích' implies achievements only; track record is neutral overall performance.

meaning: In addition to what has been said; furthermore; moreover.
example: He went to a famous school, and a good one at that.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy học một trường nổi tiếng, mà lại còn là trường tốt nữa chứ.
check note: Headword 'mà lại còn thế nữa' is awkward; example is fine.

meaning: At issue, at risk.
Vietnamese: đang đứng trước nguy cơ được mất
example: What is at stake in these next 20 minutes is the championship.
example Vietnamese: Thứ được mất trong 20 phút tới đây chính là chức vô địch.
back-translation: facing the risk of winning or losing
check note: 'Nguy cơ được mất' is unnatural and muddled; example is fine.

meaning: To make one feel comfortable, to seem appropriate or acceptable to.
Vietnamese: khiến người ta thấy ổn thỏa
example: The way you talk to your wife doesn't sit right with me.
example Vietnamese: Cái cách anh nói chuyện với vợ làm tôi thấy không ổn chút nào.
back-translation: make people feel it's all right
check note: 'Thấy ổn thỏa' is unnatural; ổn thỏa describes arrangements, not feelings.

meaning: Certainly; by all means; as a matter of importance.
Vietnamese: nhất định, không được sai sót
example: You will report to the police every week without fail.
example Vietnamese: Anh phải trình diện cảnh sát hằng tuần, tuyệt đối không được bỏ.
check note: 'Không được sai sót' means making no errors, not without fail.

meaning: To pretend or imagine.
example: Let's make believe that we are explorers.
example Vietnamese: Mình giả làm nhà thám hiểm đi.
check note: Without a comma, headword reads as 'pretend to imagine'.

meaning: Well done, to a male.
back-translation: Very good boy / what a good son
check note: Reads as 'obedient son'; loses general 'well done' to any male.

meaning: To be skilled, adept, or graceful with or at (something).
Vietnamese: rất khéo léo trong chuyện xử lý
example: She has a way with animals, and they seem instinctively to trust her.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy rất khéo với động vật, và chúng dường như tin cô theo bản năng.
check note: 'Trong chuyện xử lý' is unnatural, dangling, and narrower than 'have a way with'.

meaning: To conceal oneself; to remain hidden.
example: I'll lie low here until you get back.
example Vietnamese: Tôi sẽ nấp ở đây cho đến khi anh quay lại.
check note: 'Chờ thời' adds awaiting an opportunity; meaning is just staying hidden.

meaning: Inexperienced; just beginning; immature (especially in judgment).
check note: Stresses being newly arrived; inexperience and immature judgement are weaker.

meaning: As a profession; professionally.
example: Although he was a gifted musician, he was a plumber by trade and never played music professionally.
example Vietnamese: Dù chơi nhạc rất giỏi, anh ấy làm nghề thợ ống nước và chưa từng chơi nhạc chuyên nghiệp.
check note: 'Theo nghề nghiệp' is unnatural; reads as 'according to occupation'.

meaning: Resembling; similar to; in a way; partially or not entirely.
example: He wrote a polite retraction, as an apology of sorts for his harsh words.
example Vietnamese: Anh viết lời rút lại lịch sự, như một kiểu xin lỗi cho những lời gay gắt của mình.
check note: Example's 'viết lời rút lại' is unnatural for writing a retraction.

meaning: To play truant; to avoid (informally: skip) school, work, or other duties (stay away from these without permission nor an excuse); to skive or to bunk off (UK);
example: Plenty of people played hooky from work to go see the movie on opening day.
example Vietnamese: Rất nhiều người trốn làm để đi xem phim trong ngày công chiếu.
back-translation: to skip work to go have fun
check note: Narrowed to skipping work; omits school truancy and other duties.

meaning: Well done, to a female.
check note: Praises a daughter's obedience; misses 'well done' to a female.

meaning: Especially; more than other people
Vietnamese: không ai khác mà lại là
back-translation: none other than, of all people/things
check note: Reads as 'none other than'; 'especially, more than others' is lost.

meaning: On one's hands and knees.
Vietnamese: bò bằng tay và đầu gối
back-translation: to crawl on hands and knees
check note: Adds crawling; the meaning is just being on hands and knees.

meaning: When a valuable potential has finally unfolded into a vibrant reality.
back-translation: the most brilliant level / peak brightness
check note: Can read as peak brightness; potential unfolding into reality is lost.

meaning: To praise or congratulate.
example: Don't pat yourself on the back so vigorously; you might hurt yourself.
example Vietnamese: Đừng tự khen mình hăng quá, coi chừng đau tay đấy.
back-translation: to pat on the shoulder in praise
check note: Example drops the self-patting image, so the sore hand makes little sense.

meaning: A putting down or expression of disdain about something that one desires but cannot have.
example: I think his comments about that new car are just sour grapes because he can't afford it.
check note: Near-literal; disdain for the unattainable is unclear without the fable.

meaning: Not gradually; all at once; referring especially to quitting a habit by force of will rather than by a gradual reduction.
example: It is difficult, but possible to quit smoking cold turkey.
example Vietnamese: Bỏ thuốc lá dứt khoát một lần thì khó, nhưng làm được.
back-translation: to quit decisively once and for all
check note: Reads as 'once and for all'; abrupt, non-gradual quitting is unclear.

meaning: Exactly, to its full degree
check note: Fits only comparisons; 'exactly, to the full degree' is weakly conveyed.

meaning: (Very) inaccurate.
example: Well, I suppose you could say the weatherman was wide of the mark again then!
example Vietnamese: Chà, có thể nói anh dự báo thời tiết lại đoán trật lất rồi!
check note: Example's 'anh dự báo thời tiết' can read as addressing 'you'.

meaning: The practice of flipping a coin in the air, to choose between two alternatives based on which side lands face up.
back-translation: heads or tails (face down or face up)
check note: Gives only the call; coin-toss practice for choosing is not conveyed.

meaning: Feeling sharp anticipation or anxiety; in a state of suspense.
check note: Conveys fidgeting; anxious or eager suspense is weak.

meaning: To take the wrong approach to a situation; to follow a false lead; to attempt to solve a problem using mistaken assumptions about its true nature.
Vietnamese: nhầm hướng ngay từ cách nghĩ
back-translation: going the wrong way from the very way of thinking
check note: Awkward explanatory phrasing, not a natural Vietnamese expression.

meaning: To go unchecked; to be out of control.
back-translation: free to run wild, do as one pleases
check note: Connotes bold free rein; the 'out of control' sense is weakened.

meaning: To lessen or weaken over time, as from overuse.
example: Your jocose wisecracks have already worn thin.
example Vietnamese: Mấy câu đùa cợt của anh đã nhàm lắm rồi.
check note: Narrows to becoming boring; general lessening or weakening is lost.

meaning: A liking for foods that are sweet; a weakness for sweets.
example: He eats a healthy diet most of the time, but has a sweet tooth when it comes to candy.
example Vietnamese: Phần lớn thời gian anh ấy ăn uống lành mạnh, nhưng lại hảo ngọt khi gặp kẹo.
check note: Example phrase 'hảo ngọt khi gặp kẹo' is unnatural.

meaning: (Knowing, remembering, or understanding something) with extreme clarity, especially a painful or highly emotional experience.
check note: Means 'clearer than ever', not 'only too well'; adds a comparison.

meaning: A hierarchy.
example: With my promotion this month I will continue my steady journey to the top of the food chain.
example Vietnamese: Với lần thăng chức tháng này, tôi sẽ tiếp tục vững bước tiến lên đỉnh của thang bậc.
check note: Example's 'đỉnh của thang bậc' is unnatural Vietnamese.

meaning: Rapidly or immediately.
example: Fortunately, help arrived on the double, and the victim's injuries were soon treated.
example Vietnamese: May mà cứu hộ đến rất nhanh, vết thương của nạn nhân sớm được chữa trị.
check note: 'Nhanh lên' reads as the command 'hurry up', not an adverb.

meaning: The final cessation or discontinuance of a process, institution, lineage, or person, especially one which has existed for a considerable period of time; death.
Vietnamese: bước đường cùng, hồi kết thúc
back-translation: the end of the road, the final chapter
check note: 'Bước đường cùng' means desperate straits, not final cessation or death.

meaning: To seem to be correct, or plausible
Vietnamese: nghe có vẻ đúng, đáng tin
example: His excuse about his daughter being ill again rings true, to me.
example Vietnamese: Theo tôi, lời anh ta viện cớ con gái lại ốm nghe có vẻ thật.
check note: Example's 'viện cớ' implies a false pretext and reads awkwardly.

meaning: Not included in the matter being planned or under consideration; not a factor or participant in the present situation.
Vietnamese: không còn liên quan trong cuộc
back-translation: no longer relevant in the contest
check note: 'Không còn liên quan trong cuộc' is awkward; 'ngoài cuộc' sense unclear.

meaning: To allow to be apprehended in its full scope.
back-translation: to show oneself worthy of one's standing; perform up to par
check note: Reads as performing worthily; sense of conveying something's full scope is unclear.

meaning: Expresses that the speaker must go and deal with something.
Vietnamese: Có việc phải đi làm rồi
example: Excuse me, gentlemen, but I'm afraid duty calls.
example Vietnamese: Xin lỗi các anh, e là tôi có việc phải đi rồi.
back-translation: I've got to go to work now
check note: Headword reads as leaving for work, not attending to a duty.

meaning: Well in advance.
Vietnamese: từ xa đã nhận ra trước
back-translation: to recognize in advance from far off; see it coming
check note: Adds the verb 'recognize'; meaning is just 'well in advance'.

meaning: To return to a previous state.
example: We had a terrible year so we agreed to turn back the clock and go on as if it hadn't happened.
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi đã trải qua một năm tồi tệ nên quyết định quay lại như thể chuyện đó chưa từng xảy ra.
check note: Example 'quay lại' is ambiguous and drops 'go on'.

meaning: A moderate inclination.
Vietnamese: ý định nửa muốn nửa không
example: His behaviour gives me half a mind to throw him out.
example Vietnamese: Cách cư xử của hắn khiến tôi chỉ muốn tống cổ hắn ra ngoài.
check note: Example says 'just want to throw him out', losing the moderate inclination.

meaning: Used to liken one situation to another, typically saying that the existence of one situation is equivalent to the existence of another, usually more extreme, situation.
example: You're going to tell her what I said about her? You might as well shoot me!
example Vietnamese: Cậu định kể với cô ấy những gì tớ nói về cô ấy à? Thế thì bắn tớ luôn đi cho rồi!
check note: Headword means 'would rather do that', not likening to an extreme situation.
